rules.quote: Each of 32 independent bits can be written as peripheral outputs in two modes. In the output direction, this module provides direct 32b access to each GPIO value using direct write. This mode allows software to control all GPIO bits simultaneously.
rules.condition: writing GPIO outputs in direct-write mode
rules.statement: Each of the 32 independent GPIO bits can be written as a peripheral output via direct write, giving software simultaneous control of all 32 bits.

review.reason: Quote states direct write gives simultaneous control of all 32 bits; testable by scenario.

rules.quote: Each of 32 independent bits can be written as peripheral outputs in two modes. Alternately, this module provides masked writes to half of the bits at a time, allowing software to affect the output value of a subset of the bits without requiring a read-modify-write. In this mode the user provides a mask of which of the 16 bits are to be modified, along with their new value.
rules.condition: writing GPIO outputs in masked-write mode
rules.statement: Masked write modifies only the selected bits of a 16-bit half, using the user-provided mask and new values, without read-modify-write; unmasked bits keep their output value.

review.reason: Quote states masked write on 16-bit half with mask and no read-modify-write; the 'unmasked bits keep value' is implied by the stated purpose. Scenario check is appropriate.

rules.quote: Each of the 32 bits can be read by software as peripheral inputs. In the input direction, software can read the contents of any of the GPIO peripheral inputs.
rules.statement: Software can read each of the 32 GPIO bits as peripheral inputs.

review.reason: Quote says software can read inputs, a capability stated with 'can'; MAY is fine but the check is better as both scenario and assertion is not possible; strength correct. Actually the rule is a capability; the field MAY is right, so only actor should be corrected to slave (register read by software).

rules.quote: In addition, software can request the detection of an interrupt event for any of the 32 bits in a configurable manner. The choices are positive edge, negative edge or level detection events.
rules.condition: interrupt configured for a GPIO bit
rules.statement: Software can configure interrupt event detection for any of the 32 bits as positive edge, negative edge or level detection.

review.reason: Software-configurable interrupt detection modes (pos edge, neg edge, level) are stated; MAY for an optional configuration capability, scenario check.

rules.quote: A noise filter is available through configuration for any of the 32 GPIO inputs. This requires the input to be stable for 16 cycles of the module clock before the input register reflects the change and interrupt generation is evaluated.
rules.condition: noise filter enabled for a GPIO input
rules.statement: The input must be stable for 16 module clock cycles before the input register reflects the change and interrupt generation is evaluated.

review.reason: Quote states 16 module clock cycle stability requirement for filtered input; both scenario and assertion plausible.

rules.quote: Note that if the filter is enabled and the pin is set to output then there will be a corresponding delay in a change in output value being reflected in the input register.
rules.condition: filter enabled and pin set to output
rules.statement: A change in output value is reflected in the input register with a corresponding filter delay.

review.reason: Quote says 'there will be a corresponding delay' with filter enabled and pin as output; this is a note on expected behavior, MUST is acceptable, but the delay is not quantified; it is better left as a scenario. Strength and check kept; actor should be system.

rules.quote: The GPIO module maintains one 32-bit output register DATA_OUT with two ways to write to it. Direct write access uses DIRECT_OUT, and masked access uses MASKED_OUT_UPPER and MASKED_OUT_LOWER. Direct access provides full write and read access for all 32 bits in one register.
rules.statement: DIRECT_OUT provides full write and read access to all 32 bits of the DATA_OUT register.

review.reason: Quote states full write/read access to all 32 bits via direct access.

rules.quote: For masked access the bits to modify are given as a mask in the upper 16 bits of the MASKED_OUT_UPPER and MASKED_OUT_LOWER register write, while the data to write is provided in the lower 16 bits of the register write. The hardware updates DATA_OUT with the mask so that the modification is done without software requiring a Read-Modify-Write.
rules.condition: a write to MASKED_OUT_UPPER or MASKED_OUT_LOWER
rules.statement: Upper 16 bits of the write are a mask of bits to modify and lower 16 bits are data; hardware updates only masked DATA_OUT bits without read-modify-write.

review.reason: Mask/data split and no RMW stated.

rules.quote: Reads of masked registers return the lower/upper 16 bits of the DATA_OUT contents. Zeros are returned in the upper 16 bits (mask field).
rules.condition: a read of a masked output register
rules.statement: Reads return the upper or lower 16 bits of DATA_OUT in the lower 16 bits, with zeros in the upper 16 mask-field bits.

review.reason: Read returns half of DATA_OUT with zero upper bits.

rules.quote: The same concept is duplicated for the output enable register DATA_OE. Direct access uses DIRECT_OE, and masked access is available using MASKED_OE_UPPER and MASKED_OE_LOWER.
rules.statement: DATA_OE is accessible directly via DIRECT_OE and with masked access via MASKED_OE_UPPER and MASKED_OE_LOWER, with the same semantics as DATA_OUT.

review.reason: Quote states DATA_OE duplicates the concept with direct and masked access.

rules.quote: The output enable is sent to the pad control block to determine if the pad should drive the DATA_OUT value to the associated pin or not.
rules.statement: The output enable is sent to the pad control block to determine whether the pad drives the DATA_OUT value to the pin.

review.reason: Pad control block is outside the GPIO; output enable routing is a description. Cannot be exercised in the GPIO test alone; an output-enable-to-pad connection is only observable at the interface, so at best an assertion on oe output.

rules.quote: For GPIO outputs that are not used (either not wired to a pin output or not selected for pin multiplexing), the output values are disconnected and have no effect on the GPIO input, regardless of output enable values.
rules.condition: GPIO output is unused (not wired to a pin or not selected for pin multiplexing)
rules.statement: Output values of unused GPIOs are disconnected and have no effect on the GPIO input regardless of output enable values.

review.reason: Quote explicitly states unused outputs have no effect on input.

rules.quote: Both views alias the same state, and a write to a per-pin register only affects the GPIO it belongs to.
rules.statement: The per-pin and 32-bit register views alias the same state, and a write to a per-pin register affects only its own GPIO.

review.reason: Aliasing and per-pin write isolation stated.

rules.quote: The per-pin view consists of two separate, aligned address ranges, so access to the data of a GPIO can be granted without access to its configuration: PER_PIN_IO holds one register per GPIO with bit i of DATA_OUT and of DATA_IN. The configuration range holds two registers per GPIO, which directly follow one another: PER_PIN_OE_0 with bit 0 of DATA_OE, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_0 with bit 0 of the interrupt control and input filter registers, then PER_PIN_OE_1, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_1, and so on.
rules.statement: Per-pin view has separate aligned ranges: PER_PIN_IO holds one register per GPIO for DATA_OUT/DATA_IN bit i; configuration range holds consecutive PER_PIN_OE_n and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_n registers per GPIO.

review.reason: Register layout stated by quote.

rules.quote: A register write must cover all bytes of the register that hold a field, so access cannot be granted to only some fields of a register.
rules.statement: A register write must cover all bytes of the register that hold a field.

review.reason: Requirement on write coverage is about the bus access granularity; the register enforces it (access cannot be granted to partial fields). Actor master is a software/bus constraint; better expressed as a slave/interconnect behaviour, but the quote is a rule for the writer.

rules.quote: The interrupt registers INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST have no per-pin view.
rules.statement: INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST have no per-pin view.

review.reason: Quote states no per-pin view for these registers.

rules.quote: The DATA_IN register returns the contents as seen on the peripheral input, typically from the pads connected to those inputs. The contents of DATA_IN are always readable and reflect the value seen at the chip input pad regardless of the output enable setting from DATA_OE. If the output enable is true (and the GPIO is connected to a chip-level pad), the value read from DATA_IN includes the effect of the peripheral's driven output and will only differ from DATA_OUT if the output driver is unable to switch the pin or during the delay imposed by the input synchronizer and noise filter (if enabled).
rules.statement: DATA_IN is always readable and reflects the value at the chip input pad regardless of DATA_OE.

review.reason: DATA_IN always readable and reflects pad regardless of OE.

rules.quote: In the presence of a pin-multiplexing unit, GPIO peripheral inputs that are not connected to a chip input will be tied to a constant zero input.
rules.condition: pin-multiplexing unit present and the peripheral input is not connected to a chip input
rules.statement: GPIO peripheral inputs not connected to a chip input are tied to constant zero.

review.reason: Quote states tie-off to zero when not connected.

rules.quote: The GPIO module provides optional independent noise filter control for each of the 32 input signals. Each input can be independently enabled with the CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER (one bit per input). This 16-cycle filter is applied to both the DATA_IN register and the interrupt detection logic.
rules.statement: Each of the 32 inputs can be independently enabled for the 16-cycle noise filter via CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER, applied to both DATA_IN and interrupt detection.

review.reason: Optional per-input filter enabled by CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER.

rules.quote: The GPIO controller provides an optional feature to sample GPIO input values as hardware configuration straps. After each reset, on the first cycle when the strap_en_i signal is asserted, the GPIO detects its transition from low to high. One clock cycle later, it samples the GPIO input values and stores them in the HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN register.
rules.condition: after reset, first cycle strap_en_i is asserted
rules.statement: GPIO detects strap_en_i low-to-high and one clock cycle later samples the GPIO inputs into HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN.

review.reason: Strap sampling timing stated by quote.

rules.quote: Sampling occurs exclusively at this time, and any subsequent changes to the GPIO input configuration will not be captured. This mechanism samples all 32 bits of the GPIO input data, regardless of the GPIO output enable status, providing a reliable snapshot of the input values for firmware access.
rules.condition: after the strap sample is taken
rules.statement: All 32 input bits are sampled regardless of output enable, and later input changes are not captured in HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN.

review.reason: Sampling only once, all 32 bits regardless of OE.

rules.quote: Following the standard interrupt guidelines in the Comportability Specification, the 32 bits of the INTR_ENABLE register determines whether the associated inputs are configured to detect interrupt events. If enabled via the various INTR_CTRL_EN registers, their current state can be read in the INTR_STATE register. Note #1: The interrupt can only be triggered by GPIO input.
rules.condition: interrupt enabled via INTR_ENABLE and INTR_CTRL_EN registers
rules.statement: Interrupt state is readable in INTR_STATE only when enabled, and can be triggered only by GPIO input.

review.reason: Rule mixes two statements; 'only triggered by GPIO input' is a restriction (MUST_NOT-like for other sources) but the enablement requirement is stated. Quote supports it as written with the state readable only if enabled; keep MUST but check both scenario and assertion is not feasible.

rules.quote: Clearing is done by writing a 1 into the associated INTR_STATE bit field.
rules.statement: Writing 1 to an INTR_STATE bit clears that interrupt.

review.reason: W1C clearing stated.

rules.quote: For configuration, there are 4 types of interrupts available per bit, controlled with four control registers. INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING configures the associated input for rising-edge detection. Similarly, INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING detects falling edge inputs. INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH and INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW allow the input to be level sensitive interrupts.
rules.statement: Each bit supports rising-edge, falling-edge, level-high and level-low interrupt detection, selected by the corresponding INTR_CTRL_EN register.

review.reason: Four interrupt types stated.

rules.quote: In theory an input can be configured to detect both a rising and falling edge, but there is no hardware assistance to indicate which edge caused the output interrupt.
rules.statement: An input may be configured for both rising and falling edge detection, with no hardware indication of which edge caused the interrupt.

review.reason: Both-edge configuration allowed, stated as 'in theory'.

rules.quote: Note #2: All inputs are sent through optional noise filtering before being sent into interrupt detection.
rules.statement: All inputs pass through the optional noise filter before interrupt detection.

review.reason: Noise filter precedes interrupt detection per Note #2.

rules.quote: Note #3: All interrupts to the processor are level interrupts as per the Comportability Specification guidelines. The GPIO module, if configured, converts an edge detection into a level interrupt to the processor core.
rules.statement: Interrupts to the processor are level interrupts; edge detection is converted into a level interrupt.

review.reason: Level interrupt conversion stated.

rules.quote: Grant each component access to only the per-pin registers of its GPIOs, and keep using the 32-bit registers in software that manages all GPIOs, for example during initialization.
rules.condition: when individual GPIOs belong to different software components
rules.statement: Each component should be granted access only to the per-pin registers of its own GPIOs, while software managing all GPIOs keeps using the 32-bit registers.

review.reason: Quote states the guidance; it is a software/system-level recommendation, nothing to check in simulation (check=none).

rules.quote: PER_PIN_IO_i has fields in bytes 0 and 1, so a write to it must cover both bytes, i.e., be at least 16 bits wide.
rules.condition: when writing PER_PIN_IO_i, which has fields in bytes 0 and 1
rules.statement: A write to PER_PIN_IO_i must cover both bytes 0 and 1, i.e., be at least 16 bits wide.

review.reason: Quote states a write to PER_PIN_IO_i must cover bytes 0 and 1 (>=16 bits); it can be exercised with writes of different widths.

rules.quote: A byte write returns an error and has no effect, so a capability for PER_PIN_IO_i must cover at least these two bytes.
rules.condition: when a byte write is made to PER_PIN_IO_i
rules.statement: A byte write to PER_PIN_IO_i returns an error and has no effect on the register.

review.reason: Quote states a byte write returns an error with no effect; the slave response and unchanged register can be exercised in a scenario.

merged_from.quote: A byte write returns an error and has no effect, so a capability for PER_PIN_IO_i must cover at least these two bytes.

rules.quote: PER_PIN_OE_i and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i also accept byte writes.
rules.statement: PER_PIN_OE_i and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i accept byte writes.

review.reason: Quote says these registers 'also accept byte writes', which is a definite behavior and not optional. Strength should be MUST, and the actor is the slave, since the slave accepts the writes; a scenario check remains appropriate.

review.reason: Quote states synchronous sampling/output change at clk_i rising edge; checkable from interface signals.

review.reason: Reset assertion async and release sync is a property of the reset input driven by the environment; async assertion cannot be checked cycle-by-cycle from interface. Use scenario.

review.reason: Registers hold reset values while rst_ni low; both assertion and scenario reasonable.

questions.question: Is the filter delay exactly 16 module clock cycles when the pin is an output, and does the input register reflect output changes only after that delay? Also, is the stable-input window restarted on any glitch?
questions.note: The documents say the input must be stable for 16 module clock cycles and that with the filter on and the pin set to output, a change in output value reaches the input register with a delay. They do not say that the count restarts on a glitch. D-007 says the exact threshold is not checked; it only bounds the behaviour: a value held 12 cycles or less never appears, and one held 24 cycles or more appears within 24 cycles. The designer must define the exact count and the glitch-restart semantics.

decision.answer: Not defined by the documents. D-007 applies: the exact count and whether a glitch restarts it are not checked; tests hold a new filtered value either at most 12 cycles (must not appear) or at least 24 cycles (must appear within 24 cycles). There is no pad model (INT-IO-002, D-021): DATA_IN follows i_gpio only, so output-to-input delay is not a case here.

questions.question: Does INTR_STATE only show an interrupt when both INTR_ENABLE and an INTR_CTRL_EN bit are set, or does INTR_ENABLE only gate the output interrupt?
questions.note: The documents disagree. The GPIO text makes INTR_ENABLE a condition for detection, and the INTR_CTRL_EN descriptions say 'If INTR_ENABLE[i] is true'. The comportability text says INTR_STATE is not qualified by INTR_ENABLE and that INTR_ENABLE only masks the output. D-004 only records that the verification checks what both readings share. The designer must state the real behaviour, i.e. whether INTR_STATE[i] is set by an event while INTR_ENABLE[i]=0.

decision.answer: The documents disagree and do not decide it. Per D-004 only the common part is checked: with INTR_ENABLE[i]=1 a configured event sets INTR_STATE[i]; with INTR_ENABLE[i]=0 o_intr_gpio[i] stays 0; INTR_STATE[i] after an event while INTR_ENABLE[i]=0 is not checked. Left open for the G4 reviewer.

questions.question: What are the 'configurations of the run set'? They are not defined in the quotes.
questions.note: The run set is not defined. The documents only say the verification runs in every combination of GpioAsyncOn and GpioAsHwStrapsEn that the run set selects, with (1,1) as the default. Which of the four combinations belong to the run set must be decided by the designer or project owner.

decision.answer: All four combinations are in the run set: base (GpioAsyncOn=1, GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1, two seeds), sync_off (0,1), straps_off (1,0) and min (0,0), one seed each.

questions.question: MASKED_OE_* bits 31:16 are unchecked because the text says 0 and the field table says rw; should the designer settle which is correct?
questions.note: The documents conflict: the register text says the read-back upper 16 bits are zero, while the field table lists mask bits 31:16 as rw. D-002 only leaves bits 31:16 unchecked. The designer must settle which is correct.

decision.answer: Not settled by the documents; D-002 stands (bits 31:16 of a MASKED_OE_* read are not checked; bits 15:0 are). Left open for the G4 reviewer.

questions.question: Does 'no later than 4 cycles after the first rising edge' include or exclude that edge, and does it apply to the register read value or an internal flop? The latency bounds depend on this.
questions.note: The documents do not define the counting convention, i.e. whether the 4 cycles are counted from or after the first rising edge, nor whether the bound applies to the DATA_IN register read value or an internal flop. D-018 only says 'no later than 4 cycles after the first rising edge after the change' for DATA_IN. The designer must define the reference point and the observation point.

decision.answer: Counting convention for D-018: let E0 be the first rising edge of clk_i at which i_gpio already has the new value. The bound is observed at the ports: a Get of DATA_IN accepted (a_valid and a_ready) at E0+4 or later returns the new value; likewise an INTR_STATE read accepted at E0+8 or later (filter off) shows the event, and o_intr_gpio follows D-018. Internal flops are never observed.

questions.question: Can a status-type interrupt's INTR_STATE bit be read-only and follow the input directly, and does INTR_TEST still apply to it? The quote doesn't say.
questions.note: The documents say that for status type interrupts INTR_STATE has ro access and the wired interrupt comes from the input, qualified only by INTR_ENABLE. They do not say whether INTR_STATE follows the input directly or whether INTR_TEST applies to a status interrupt. The designer must decide (the GPIO interrupts are event type, so this is out of scope for GPIO).

decision.answer: Out of scope: all gpio interrupts are event type (Hardware Interfaces, Interrupts table). Status-type interrupt rules are not verified for this design.

questions.question: How long may a protocol lock-up persist before the pingfail alert must fire, i.e. what is the bound on 'eventually'?
questions.note: The documents only say that a lock-up eventually triggers a signal integrity alert or a pingfail alert. The ping timeout is programmable and the ping spacing is randomized, and no bound is given for 'eventually'. In this wrapper pings are never issued. The designer must specify the bound if it is to be checked.

decision.answer: Out of scope: the wrapper never issues ping requests (INT-CFG-003), so ping timeouts and pingfail are not checked.

questions.question: When a sender-side encoding error is signalled by alert_p/n being set to the same value and toggling, is the toggling period specified?
questions.note: The documents only say the alert_p/n wires are set to the same value and that value is continuously toggled. No toggle period is specified for the alert path (the 'toggled each cycle' wording belongs to the escalation path). The designer must specify the period if it is to be checked.

decision.answer: Not checked: the sender-side encoding error signalling is not observable at the ports except through o_alert_integ_fail, which a correct sender never sets (INT-ALERT-002, D-017); no toggle period is checked.

answered_questions.question: In masked write, which half (upper/lower) is selected and how are the mask and data fields laid out? Does the quote define this?
answered_questions.answer: MASKED_OUT_LOWER (and MASKED_OE_LOWER) controls bits 15:0 of DATA_OUT (DATA_OE). MASKED_OUT_UPPER (and MASKED_OE_UPPER) controls bits 31:16. In the register write, the upper 16 bits (31:16) are the mask and the lower 16 bits (15:0) are the data. A bit is updated only where its mask bit is 1.

answered_questions.question: Is the interrupt noise filter path (CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER) optional per input, and how does the 'MUST pass through filter' rule relate to it being optional?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. The noise filter is optional and independently enabled per input through CTRL_EN_INPUT_FILTER. The 16-cycle filter applies to both DATA_IN and interrupt detection when enabled. 'All inputs go through the filter' therefore means each input passes through the optional filter stage, which is active only where its enable bit is 1.

answered_questions.question: Is the error response for a byte write to PER_PIN_IO_i a bus error response, and does it apply to every kind of access (e.g., a capability-checked access versus a plain write)? Also, what does a write of 16 bits or more that is not aligned to bytes 0-1 do?
answered_questions.answer: A write narrower than the register's fields is rejected: a byte write to PER_PIN_IO_i returns an error (d_error=1) and has no effect, so a write must cover both bytes 0 and 1 (at least 16 bits). Hardware sees only the bus access, so the error is independent of any capability check; the capability must simply cover those two bytes. PER_PIN_OE_i and PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i accept byte writes. For the register tool, 8b or 16b writes that are not 4B-aligned also return an error. A 16-bit write at the wrong byte lane is therefore an error.

answered_questions.question: Registers list reset 'x' for PER_PIN_OE/INTR_CTRL fields but the note for indices 1..31 says reset default 0x0; which is correct?
answered_questions.answer: The 'Reset default' line binds: PER_PIN_OE_i, PER_PIN_INTR_CTRL_i and PER_PIN_IO_i.data_out read 0 after reset. The 'x' in the field tables is overridden, and indices 1..31 follow GPIO[0] with reset default 0x0.

answered_questions.question: Is the snapshot taken on the strap_en rising edge, on level high, or on a specific cycle, and how many cycles after the event do sampled_straps values become valid?
answered_questions.answer: The snapshot is triggered by the low-to-high transition (rising edge) of strap_en_i, not by the level. The GPIO detects the transition on the first cycle strap_en_i is asserted after reset and samples the inputs one clock cycle later, storing them in HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN. The bound used by the verification is that the valid indications read 1 within 4 cycles after the edge.

answered_questions.question: Can a later strap_en assertion (for example after reset) trigger a new snapshot, given that behaviour after the event 'has no effect'?
answered_questions.answer: Within one reset period, sampling occurs only once and later changes are not captured. After each reset the GPIO detects the transition again, so a new strap_en rising edge after a reset triggers a new snapshot.

answered_questions.question: What are the exact interrupt modes (rising, falling, level high/low) and the latency from detection to the interrupt event?
answered_questions.answer: There are four modes per bit: rising edge (INTR_CTRL_EN_RISING), falling edge (INTR_CTRL_EN_FALLING), level high (INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLHIGH) and level low (INTR_CTRL_EN_LVLLOW). No exact latency is given. D-018 bounds it: INTR_STATE is set no later than 4 cycles after the event appears in DATA_IN, and o_intr_gpio equals INTR_STATE AND INTR_ENABLE except in the 2 cycles after either changes. Lower bounds are not checked.

answered_questions.question: Is the pass-through of GpioAsyncOn/GpioAsHwStrapsEn something to be checked (e.g. by elaboration), or only a configuration note? What is the observable behaviour for each value?
answered_questions.answer: The two parameters are passed through unchanged from gpio to ot_gpio_nnc. Verification runs in the combinations the run set selects. GpioAsyncOn=1 instantiates 2-flop synchronizers on the inputs, so i_gpio may change at any time; 0 means no synchronizer and i_gpio changes only synchronously to clk_i. GpioAsHwStrapsEn=0 makes HW_STRAPS_DATA_IN read 0, with the valid and data outputs unchecked. GpioAsHwStrapsEn=1 samples straps as described in D-008. The documents do not call for an elaboration check.

answered_questions.question: Which signals identify a ping request, and in which block should the 'never issued' property be checked?
answered_questions.answer: A ping request is the receiver's ping_req_i assertion, which appears as a level change on alert_rx.ping_p/n towards the sender. The configuration states that ping requests are never issued. This property concerns the wrapper's alert receiver, which connects to gpio's alert sender.

answered_questions.question: Which actor drives i_gpio and rst_ni (test bench vs. system), and are the INT-CLK-002 and GpioAsyncOn = 0 constraints environment assumptions rather than DUT checks?
answered_questions.answer: The test bench drives i_gpio, which depends on nothing in the DUT. The test bench also resets the design. The INT-CLK-002 rule (with GpioAsyncOn=0, i_gpio changes only synchronously to clk_i) is a constraint on the test bench stimulus, an environment assumption rather than a DUT check. With GpioAsyncOn=1, i_gpio may change at any time. rst_ni is asserted asynchronously and released synchronously to clk_i.

answered_questions.question: GP-2-02 says all outputs change only at the rising clk_i edge except for rst_ni; does that exception cover asynchronous reset assertion forcing outputs low immediately, and does i_gpio with GpioAsyncOn=1 pass through a synchronizer to outputs?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. The edge-only rule has the exception of rst_ni's effect. While rst_ni is 0, the listed outputs are 0, and the rule is not applied in cycles where rst_ni is 0 or falls. With GpioAsyncOn=1 the inputs pass through 2-flop synchronizers before reaching DATA_IN, which adds delay, and D-018 bounds this by 4 cycles after the first rising edge when the filter is off.

answered_questions.question: Is o_gpio always equal to DATA_OUT combinationally, or is there a register delay or masking (e.g. MASKED_OUT_*)? The timing of equality affects any assertion.
answered_questions.answer: o_gpio is DATA_OUT and o_gpio_en is DATA_OE. DATA_OUT is updated by the direct or masked write, and the masked write is applied by hardware without read-modify-write. The only timing stated is a bound: o_gpio and o_gpio_en equal DATA_OUT and DATA_OE no later than 2 cycles after the response of the write that changed them. Lower bounds are not checked, so a purely combinational path is not required.

answered_questions.question: Is o_alert / o_alert_integ_fail a level or a pulse, and is it sticky until cleared? Latency from the alert event is not specified.
answered_questions.answer: o_alert is a pulse: it is 1 for one clock cycle per alert handshake detected by the receiver, and it is not sticky. o_alert_integ_fail is the receiver's integ_fail_o and a correct sender never raises it (D-017: 0 whenever rst_ni=1). Latency: a write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault gives exactly one o_alert pulse no later than 16 cycles after the write response. After an accepted request with i_a_intg_flip=1, o_alert pulses within 16 cycles.

answered_questions.question: Is o_d_intg_err valid every cycle or only on a D-channel valid beat?
answered_questions.answer: o_d_intg_err is 1 only in a cycle where o_d_valid is 1 and the response integrity check fails. In all other cycles it is 0. A correct device never makes it 1, and it shall be 0 in every cycle with rst_ni=1.

answered_questions.question: Is a_user.rsvd and a_user.instr_type observable at the wrapper's ports, or only internally? This decides whether GP-4.1-02 and GP-4.1-03 can be checked every cycle from interface signals.
answered_questions.answer: Only instr_type is tied to a port: i_a_instr=1 gives MuBi4True and 0 gives MuBi4False. a_user.rsvd is fixed to 0 inside the wrapper and has no port. The bit layout of a_user/d_user and the user-bit defaults are not checked.

answered_questions.question: The integrity generator code is not part of the spec and the Bus Integrity Scheme section is not written. How should correct cmd_intg and data_intg be checked, and what does a rsp_intg check failure mean?
answered_questions.answer: The test bench does not compute or check cmd_intg/data_intg. The wrapper's generator produces them, and the generator code and the Bus Integrity Scheme section are not part of the specification. i_a_intg_flip=0 means correct integrity and i_a_intg_flip=1 inverts bit 0 of cmd_intg. A rsp_intg check failure is reported as o_d_intg_err=1 (response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong). A correct device never produces it, and it shall be 0 whenever rst_ni=1.

answered_questions.question: Does 'repeated until reset' in GP-5-05 specify a repetition period, or only that o_alert pulses more than once? Also, does the bus integrity fault alert persist through the ALERT_TEST path (GP-5-06 'one alert event' versus repeating)?
answered_questions.answer: The documents state a bound rather than an exact period. A fatal alert repeats until reset. After an accepted request with i_a_intg_flip=1, o_alert pulses within 16 cycles and then at least once in every 32 cycles until rst_ni is asserted. A write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers only one alert event (exactly one o_alert pulse), so the bus integrity fault alert repeats while the ALERT_TEST path does not.

answered_questions.question: Programmer's Guide examples assume weak pull-ups on pads while INT-IO-002 says no pad model exists: must the testbench model pads (i_gpio = o_gpio where o_gpio_en=1, else 1) or is any i_gpio stimulus acceptable?
answered_questions.answer: Any i_gpio stimulus is acceptable. There is no pad model, and i_gpio is driven only by the test bench and is independent of o_gpio/o_gpio_en. A test that follows the Programmer's Guide example models the pad itself, but that is the test's choice. DATA_IN follows i_gpio only.

answered_questions.question: INT-VER-001 is truncated after 'instruction fetches, integrity errors'. Is the fatal_fault alert really part of the list, and is anything else required?
answered_questions.answer: The quote is not truncated in the document. The full list ends with 'bus error responses (unmapped addresses, sub-word writes, instruction fetches, integrity errors) and the fatal_fault alert'. So the fatal_fault alert is part of the scope and nothing else follows.

answered_questions.question: INT-VER-002 says per-pin registers 'behave alike'. Does this mean the testbench must demonstrate equivalence on all 32 GPIOs, given that the selection clause allows fewer?
answered_questions.answer: No. The verification may check every GPIO for the 32-bit registers and only a selection of GPIOs for the per-pin registers, provided the selection includes GPIO[0], GPIO[15], GPIO[16] and GPIO[31]. Demonstrating equivalence on all 32 per-pin registers is not required.

answered_questions.question: Behaviour for a new i_gpio value held between 13 and 23 cycles with the filter enabled is unspecified; is any outcome acceptable, including interrupt events?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. For a new value held between 13 and 23 cycles with the filter on, the documents define no required outcome, because the exact threshold is not checked. Only two cases are specified: a value held 12 cycles or less never appears in DATA_IN and creates no event, and a value held 24 cycles or more appears no later than 24 cycles after the change. Any outcome in the window is acceptable for the verification, including an event.

answered_questions.question: What is the project-specific default value that a baseline source drives on the user signals? It is unspecified, so the check cannot be concrete.
answered_questions.answer: The default value is not specified: a baseline source generates a project-specific default. D-022 states that user-bit default values are not checked, so no concrete check exists.

answered_questions.question: Does 'no burst transactions' mean every request is a single beat, so the size field never exceeds the bus width? Please define the checkable condition.
answered_questions.answer: Yes. Transactions are single-beat with sizes up to the bus width (byte, 2B, 4B), and there are no bursts. For this 32-bit bus, a_size must not be greater than 2 (a_size 3 is an error that devices flag with d_error). The checkable condition is a_size <= 2 for valid requests.

answered_questions.question: Is a_size>2 an error condition on the host side (must not issue) or a device d_error behaviour, given 64b support is mentioned as 'h3 in TL-UL?
answered_questions.answer: It is a device behaviour: devices have hardware protocol checkers that raise d_error when a_size is greater than 2. In this project, a request violating this is legal stimulus from the test bench, and the device answers with d_error=1. The 'h3 size is only for a 64b bus width if/when supported.

answered_questions.question: Hosts only assert a restricted mask set, yet devices may error on non-contiguous masks; which is authoritative for testing?
answered_questions.answer: They are not in conflict, since each statement addresses a different actor. Hosts in the project only assert a restricted mask set, while devices may or may not support sub-word masks and may assert d_error. For this DUT the test bench is the host and D-013 decides what is checked: full-word writes with mask 1111 succeed, and aligned byte writes (mask 0001) behave per register as stated in D-013. Other sub-word and partial-mask cases, including non-contiguous masks, are not checked.

answered_questions.question: The INTR_STATE W1C clear: if the event is still active the bit returns to true. Does it re-set on the next cycle or only on a new event edge?
answered_questions.answer: After a W1C clear with the event still active, INTR_STATE returns to true: the clear has effect for one cycle, then the bit returns to 1 after one cycle as the d input is still 1 (it does not wait for a new edge). For the GPIO level case, D-005 bounds it: INTR_STATE reads 1 and o_intr_gpio is 1 again within 4 cycles after the write response, and a dip in between is not checked.

answered_questions.question: Is the intr_o definition 'INTR_STATE AND INTR_ENABLE' valid for status interrupts, where it is derived directly from the input?
answered_questions.answer: No. The AND of INTR_STATE with INTR_ENABLE is the event type implementation. A status type interrupt creates the wired interrupt directly from the input signal, qualified only by INTR_ENABLE.

answered_questions.question: Unmapped-address errors are only 'typical'; should a testbench require an error or accept either response?
answered_questions.answer: For this DUT an error is required. D-012 states that a request to an unmapped offset in 0x000..0x3FF returns d_error=1 and changes no register. The register tool's 'may/typically' wording is generic. The TL-UL specification also lists accesses to non-existent addresses as error cases. Requests at 0x400 and above are not used.

answered_questions.question: Sub-word write errors (MUST) vs. window relaxation allowing unaligned sub-word writes without error: which governs for windows?
answered_questions.answer: They apply to different things. For register files, sub-word writes smaller than the register and unaligned writes of 8b/16b return an error. For windows, error handling belongs to the logic that manages that window's bus. Following the same rules is only recommended, and the rule may be relaxed, for example when the termination is a memory handling byte writes via masking. The window relaxation therefore governs windows only, not registers.

answered_questions.question: Is qe one cycle earlier for hwext than for non-hwext, and how does that interact with the registered we definition?
answered_questions.answer: Yes. For hwext registers the qe timing is one cycle earlier than in the non-hwext model. In the non-hwext model, qe is a registered version of the bus write-enable we, so its rising edge aligns with the change of the q output. The hwext qe is not delayed in that way.

answered_questions.question: How are the 2 wait cycles between handshakes counted, and does it depend on the clock mode (sync vs async)?
answered_questions.answer: The pause between handshakes is 2 sender clock cycles (the same constant 2 sender cycles is quoted for the collision delay). The protocol is the same in synchronous and asynchronous mode. The only difference is that the synchronizer flops at the pair inputs may be omitted in the synchronous scheme, which lowers latency.
